text: Answer the Following. Suryodaya Renewables Ltd, a listed company engaged in operating solar power plants prepares its financial statements in accordance with Indian Accounting Standards. The company owns a solar power unit located in Rajasthan, recognised as Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) in its books. As at 31 March 2025, the carrying amount of the solar unit is ₹220 crore. On 28 March 2025, Suryodaya Renewables Ltd entered into an agreement with GreenGrid Energy Solutions Pvt Ltd, under which: Legal title of the solar unit is transferred to GreenGrid Energy Solutions Pvt Ltd for a consideration of ₹200 crore. Suryodaya Renewables Ltd has the right to repurchase the solar unit after five years at a pre-determined price. During the five-year period, Suryodaya Renewables Ltd: Continues to operate and maintain the solar unit Bears all risks related to output variability, repairs, and regulatory changes Is entitled to retain all revenue generated from sale of electricity GreenGrid Energy Solutions Pvt Ltd is entitled only to a fixed annual return, irrespective of the plant’s performance. Management has derecognised the solar unit from its Balance Sheet and recognised the difference between consideration received and carrying amount as a loss on sale. The transaction is described as an “asset sale” in the notes to accounts. The statutory auditors have expressed concern regarding the derecognition of the asset. With reference to Ind AS 1 and the Conceptual Framework, examine whether derecognition of the solar unit by Suryodaya Renewables Ltd is appropriate.
